key_insight: The paper reframes the quantum fault-tolerance threshold theorem as a statement about resource-bounded objective probability: logical states are “likely” when they remain cheap to realize under available energy-and-time resources.
engineering_relevance: For FTQC design, the key question becomes measurable overhead per decade of logical-error suppression, making calibration, decoding, time budget, and ancilla management part of the engineering cost model.
method: Reinterpret objective probability using resource requirements rather than subjective belief.
Translate fault-tolerant feasibility into watts per decade of suppressed logical error.
Account for previously omitted error-correction costs: calibration, decoding, coherence time, and entropy flush.
evidence_signal: The abstract says the published record already contains the first data points for this watts-per-decade translation and identifies two measurements needed to test it empirically.
watch_item: The framework depends on how resource costs are defined and measured, so results may be sensitive to device model, noise assumptions, and uncounted overheads.
paper_title: The Threshold Theorem in Watts: Fault Tolerance as a Question About Objective Probability
